input: In the git repository /home/eval/reports, `make` builds build/report.txt from data/*.csv using the awk scripts in lib/ and data/regions.map. After recent commits the report is stale and `make` says there is nothing to do. Fix the Makefile so that build/report.txt is rebuilt whenever anything it is derived from changes, including when a new data/*.csv file is added; `make test` checks this with `make -q` on a scratch copy. Do not edit tests/, lib/ or data/. Then run plain `make` so build/report.txt is current, and commit the Makefile with a message starting with `build:`.

transcript.final_response:
I fixed the Makefile so `build/report.txt` is rebuilt whenever anything it's made from changes. `make test` passes, plain `make` rebuilt the report, and the Makefile is committed.

**Why the report was stale:**
- The list of data files was written into the Makefile (`eu` and `us` only), so the newly added `data/apac.csv` was never included.
- None of the build rules listed `lib/sum.awk`, `lib/fmt.awk` or `data/regions.map` as inputs, so editing them didn't trigger a rebuild. That's why the recent region renames and the CSV header change were missed.

**What the Makefile does now:**
- It finds every `data/*.csv` automatically and makes one `build/<name>.sum` from each, so a newly added CSV is picked up.
- Each `.sum` file is rebuilt when its CSV, `lib/sum.awk` or the Makefile changes.
- `build/report.txt` is rebuilt when any `.sum` file, `lib/fmt.awk`, `data/regions.map` or the Makefile changes.
- The report command now lists the `.sum` files explicitly instead of taking all of the rule's inputs, so the awk script and Makefile aren't fed into it as data.

**Results:**
- `make` rebuilt `apac.sum`, `eu.sum`, `us.sum` and `report.txt`, now with Japan and Australia and the new region names. The report matches `tests/expected-report.txt` exactly, and a second `make` says there's nothing to do.
- `make test` prints PASS: changing any input makes the report out of date, and a new `data/latam.csv` is detected and appears in the report.
- Commit message: `build: derive sums from all data/*.csv and depend on awk scripts, regions.map and Makefile`. Only the Makefile was committed; `tests/`, `lib/` and `data/` are unchanged.

**Two things you might want to clean up:**
- `build/report.txt`, `eu.sum` and `us.sum` are tracked in git, but the new `build/apac.sum` and the test's scratch files (`build/deps-check/`, `build/test-report.txt`) are untracked. I didn't commit them. You may want to add `build/` to `.gitignore` and stop tracking the generated files.
- `git status` didn't list the rebuilt `build/report.txt` as modified, and git in this environment gives simplified output. I can't be sure whether the tracked copy in git matches the regenerated one. If you want the stored copy updated too, it needs its own commit.

# Every data/*.csv (except non-csv files like regions.map) contributes a sum.
CSVS := $(wildcard data/*.csv)

test:

.PHONY: all test
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# Checks the Makefile dependency graph with `make -q` on a scratch copy:
# touching any input must make build/report.txt out of date.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
t=build/deps-check
inputs="lib/sum.awk lib/fmt.awk data/regions.map data/eu.csv data/us.csv data/apac.csv"
rm -rf "$t"; mkdir -p "$t"
cp -R Makefile lib data "$t"/
make -s -C "$t" build/report.txt > /dev/null || { echo "FAIL: make build/report.txt"; exit 1; }
cmp -s tests/expected-report.txt "$t/build/report.txt" || { echo "FAIL: report differs from tests/expected-report.txt"; exit 1; }
reset() {
  (cd "$t" && touch -d '2001-01-01 00:00:00' Makefile $inputs \
    && touch -d '2002-01-01 00:00:00' build/*.sum \
    && touch -d '2002-01-01 00:00:01' build/report.txt)
}
reset
make -q -C "$t" build/report.txt || { echo "FAIL: fresh build is not up to date"; exit 1; }
fail=0
for f in $inputs; do
  reset
  touch -d '2003-01-01 00:00:00' "$t/$f"
  if make -q -C "$t" build/report.txt; then
    echo "FAIL: touching $f leaves build/report.txt up to date"; fail=1
  else
    echo "ok   $f"
  fi
done
reset
printf 'region,amount\nBR,7\n' > "$t/data/latam.csv"
if make -q -C "$t" build/report.txt; then echo "FAIL: new data/latam.csv not picked up"; fail=1; fi
make -s -C "$t" build/report.txt > /dev/null
grep -q '^BR ' "$t/build/report.txt" || { echo "FAIL: data/latam.csv missing from the report"; fail=1; }
if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then echo PASS | tee build/test-report.txt; else echo FAIL > build/test-report.txt; exit 1; fi
